question: Where is Morgan Stanley investing in technology for its advisors?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base, with CEO Ted Pick stating the firm continues to invest in each of its three business segments via human capital and technology.
items.quote: We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology. Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick described AI co-piloting work in wealth management, where Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein is spending time on 'corridors or super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness for financial advisers, giving them historical context of past client interactions.
items.quote: you can have the historical context as between the financial adviser and the client where she is well aware of the past interactions... And so that co-piloting, I think, is something that Jed Finn under the leadership of Andy Saperstein is spending a lot of time on where they effectively have corridors or super agents that are going to be working to drive, again, efficiency and effectiveness across the portfolio in wealth.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with the firm's financial advisors.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley said it has ongoing investments in automation and AI and in assessing where it wants its people for the next five to ten years, in the context of a 3% reduction in its XFA (financial advisor) headcount.
items.quote: We have ongoing investments in automation, AI, and assessing where we want our people for the next five, 10 years.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's 10-K states its Wealth Management segment's ability to compete is affected by, among other factors, 'our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.'
items.quote: our ability to effectively compete against many of our competitors across different channels (i.e., advisor led, workplace and digital direct) is affected by multiple factors including our brand and reputation, the breadth, depth and pricing of our product offerings and our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.

cells.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's AI and automation initiatives directed at financial advisors, including LeadIQ, co-piloting work in wealth, and investment in AI tools throughout the enterprise.
